detail: 90 readings reported in order with correct temperatures
finalText:
Root cause and fix are done and verified on the board.

## Root cause

`sensor_task` formatted each reading into a **single stack buffer** (`char line[48]`) that it reused for every sample, then sent `&line` through the queue:

```c
char *msg = line;
xQueueSend(readings, &msg, ...);
```

The queue stored only *pointers*, and all of them pointed at the same memory. By the time `report_task` ran (after its 30 ms upload delay), the sensor had already overwritten the buffer with later readings in the burst. So each burst printed its **last** reading N times — `report seq=4 temp=21.48` ×5, `seq=9 temp=20.33` ×5, etc. — instead of seq 0,1,2,3,4 with their own temperatures.

## What I changed (`main/main.c`)

- Added a `reading_t { uint32_t seq; int temp_centi; }` struct and made the queue hold readings **by value**, so each queued entry owns a copy of its data (no aliasing).
- `sensor_task` now builds a `reading_t` and sends it; `report_task` receives it and prints it.
- Kept `FIFO_BURST = 5`, `BURST_INTERVAL_MS = 500`, and the exact `report seq=<n> temp=<t>` format unchanged.

## Verification (re-flashed, serial capture)

```
report seq=0 temp=20.00
report seq=1 temp=20.37
report seq=2 temp=20.74
report seq=3 temp=21.11
report seq=4 temp=21.48
report seq=5 temp=21.85
...
```

Every reading is now reported exactly once, in order, each with its own distinct temperature — no duplicates and no drops.
